parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
A potential difference of $2.5\text{ kV}$ is applied across a pair of horizontal metal plates in a vacuum, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}

Each plate has a length of $5.9\text{ cm}$. The separation of the plates is $4.0\text{ cm}$. The arrangement produces a uniform electric field between the plates. Assume the field does not extend beyond the edges of the plates.

An electron enters the field at point A with horizontal velocity $3.7 \times 10^7\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a line mid-way between the plates. The electron leaves the field at point B.
parts.text:
Calculate the time taken for the electron to move from A to B.

time taken = ................... . s

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the magnitude of the electric field strength.

field strength = ................... . N C⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Show that the acceleration of the electron in the field is $1.1 \times 10^{16}\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
Use the acceleration given in **(iii)** and your answer in **(i)** to determine the vertical distance $y$ between point B and the upper plate.

y = ................... . cm

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text: Explain why the calculation in **(iv)** does not need to include the gravitational effects on the electron.

parts.label: (b)(vi)
parts.text:
The electron enters the field at time $t = 0$.

On Fig. 2.2, sketch graphs to show the variation with time $t$ of

1. the horizontal component $v_{X}$ of the velocity of the electron,

2. the vertical component $v_{Y}$ of the velocity of the electron.

Numerical values are not required.

{{figure:figure_2_2.png}}
